answer: At dawn each new agent must stake a small deposit before it can trade, and that stake stays locked while its reputation grows like a vine, branching only through verifiable work with real peers. A sybil attacker who spawns thousands of identities faces a dune of cost: every fake identity needs its own stake and its own history of useful work, so flooding the network costs more than any single scam can return, while honest agents earn their stake back quickly.
